title: Clay G6 Vector-Governed Invariant-Confluent Control
summary: Open G6 architecture delta replacing scalar causal budget with vector control and effect-only closure with authority-plus-invariant-confluence closure; adds root-bound state-aware ClayCode, intervention-first dual workspace and feedback-governed edge inference.
open_questions: Does a vector governor outperform scalar/hierarchical control on real FRANK traces?
Which FRANK state classes are invariant-confluent?
Do receipt-defined and latent workspaces share function-specific causal mediation?
Does root-bound state-aware ClayCode improve pinned Qwen3-4B end-to-end?
Can a sustained Android governor improve useful work per joule without quality loss?
